- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is trending upward, reduce slope slightly to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is flat or rising, introduce downward bias to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (true > 90), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 95→90→85), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to anticipate 1–2 day pullback.  
- When sentiment is high and forecast is low, model underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid linear extrapolation — introduce curvature or volatility decay if sentiment is volatile.
